summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with acute hypercarbic respiratory failure due to tracheal occlusion from a fibrous clot, occurring the day after a prior discharge. He has a complex history of Ruvalcaba-Myhre-Smith syndrome and relapsing polychondritis with recurrent tracheal stenosis, requiring multiple prior dilations and a tracheostomy. He underwent urgent bronchoscopy and tracheal dilation, which relieved the obstruction. His elevated white count and lactate improved with supportive care and antibiotics. An acid-fast bacillus was cultured from BAL, but TB was ruled out; etanercept was held pending further evaluation. He was treated with a course of Augmentin, started on a prednisone taper, and maintained on Bactrim prophylaxis. A swallow study showed mild oropharyngeal dysphagia without aspiration, allowing return to baseline diet. He was discharged home with services on a steroid taper, antibiotics, and instructions to restart methotrexate after antibiotic completion.
